1. (Currently amended) A method, comprising: inputting database constructs generated by a database optimizer as an input to a trained machine-learning algorithm __that has been trained on historical database operations and their actual execution performance metrics__; obtaining a database operation predictor from the machine-learning algorithm as an output __wherein the database operation predictor comprises a predicted performance metric that differs from cost estimates provided by the database optimizer__; modifying at least one of the database constructs based on the database operation predictor producing a modified database construct __wherein the modification is performed prior to query execution and is based on predicted performance rather than optimizer cost estimates__; and processing a database operation with the database constructs and the modified database construct.

2. (Previously presented)

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein obtaining further includes acquiring the database operation predictor as an estimated Central Process Unit (CPU) execution time __derived from machine-learning analysis of historical execution patterns__ for one or more Access Module Processors to execute when processing the database operation.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein obtaining further includes acquiring the database operation predictor as an estimated number of Input/Output (I/O) operations __derived from machine-learning analysis of historical execution patterns__ performed by one or more Access Module Processors during execution when processing the database operation.

7. (Previously presented)

8. (Previously presented)

9. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein modifying further includes changing a workgroup assigned to the database operation as the modified database construct __based on predicted resource utilization from the machine-learning algorithm__.

10. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 further comprising, storing the database operation predictor __and the basis for the prediction__ in database statistics associated with the database operation and the database constructs.

12. (Currently amended) A method comprising: training a machine-learning algorithm with database constructs produced by a database optimizer __and corresponding actual execution performance data__; receiving query execution plans for a query from the database optimizer with a least cost query execution plan identified by the database optimizer for the query; providing the query execution plans as input to the machine-learning algorithm; obtaining as an output a predicted execution time for the query __derived from machine-learning analysis rather than optimizer cost models__ based on the least cost query execution plan; and modifying one of: the least cost query execution plan for the query, a scheduled execution time for the query, and resources that are used to execute the query based on the predicted execution time __when the predicted execution time indicates a performance characteristic that differs from the optimizer's cost estimate__.

15. (Currently amended) The method of claim 12, wherein providing further includes providing the database tool within a workload scheduler and management component of a database system __that uses the machine-learning predictions to optimize workload distribution__.

16. (Previously presented)

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 12, wherein modifying further includes changing an execution resource of the least cost query execution plan based on the predicted query execution time __derived from machine-learning analysis__ and a current performance associated with the execution resource.

19. (Currently amended) A system, comprising: a database management system; at least one hardware processor; a non-transitory computer-readable storage medium having executable instructions representing a trained machine-learning algorithm __trained on historical database operations and their actual execution performance metrics__; the machine learning algorithm configured to execute on the at least one hardware processor from the non-transitory computer-readable storage medium and to perform processing to: i) receive as input database constructs produced by a database optimizer for a database operation of the database management system; and ii) provide as output a predicted value __derived from machine-learning analysis of historical execution patterns__ relevant to one of: one or more of the database constructs and the database operation __wherein the predicted value differs from cost estimates provided by the database optimizer__; wherein the database management system is configured to process the predicted value to determine whether to modify one of: the one or more database constructs and the database operation before processing the database operation within the database management system.

20. (Previously presented)
